description: First web interface for Family Pulse. Browse accounts and transactions, assign categories, manage category rules, and toggle transfer visibility. Accessible via Tailscale tailnet at /pulse/. This is the 'see the data' milestone.

timing.gatingCondition: Feature 1 complete — transaction data flowing and queryable in PostgreSQL.

principles: Read-first UI — browsing and understanding data before any editing workflows
Mobile-friendly — Alex and Eric will check this on iPhones via Tailscale
Category assignment should be fast — single-click or minimal friction
Transfer toggle is prominent — users must see the impact of transfer filtering on totals
Consistent styling with sibling apps (Tailwind CDN, clean layout)

techStack.language: Node.js + vanilla JS (server-rendered HTML with client-side interactivity)
techStack.runtime: Express.js with EJS or Handlebars templates
techStack.testing: Jest for API endpoint tests, Playwright for critical UI flows

userStories.title: Account list view
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard shows all connected accounts grouped by member (Eric, Alex, Kids)
Each account displays: institution name, account name (masked), type, current balance
Total liquid balance displayed prominently (checking + savings)
Total revolving credit balance displayed (credit card balances owed)
Net liquid position: liquid assets minus credit card balances
Balances refresh on page load from database (no live Plaid call)
userStories.testStrategy: API endpoint tests for /api/accounts. UI test: page loads, accounts display with correct grouping.

userStories.title: Transaction list with filtering
acceptanceCriteria: Paginated transaction list (50 per page) sorted by date descending
Each row: date, merchant/name, amount (color-coded debit/credit), account, category badge
Filter by: account (dropdown), date range (start/end), category (dropdown), search text (merchant name)
Toggle: show/hide transfers (default: hidden)
Running total displayed changes with filters applied
Pending transactions visually distinguished (italic or badge)
userStories.testStrategy: API endpoint tests for /api/transactions with filter params. Pagination test. Transfer toggle test: totals change when transfers shown/hidden.

userStories.title: Category assignment UI
acceptanceCriteria: Click transaction row to open category assignment
Dropdown of all categories with color swatches
Assigning category persists immediately via API call
Option to 'Create rule: always categorize [merchant] as [category]'
Bulk categorize: select multiple transactions, assign same category
Uncategorized transactions have a visual indicator
userStories.testStrategy: API tests for PUT /api/transactions/:id/category. Rule creation test. Bulk assignment test.

userStories.title: Category CRUD admin
acceptanceCriteria: Admin page to list, create, edit, and delete categories
Category fields: name, color (hex picker), monthly budget amount, is_income flag, is_transfer_class flag, icon (optional emoji)
Cannot delete category if transactions are assigned to it (must reassign first)
Default categories seeded: Uncategorized, Income, Transfer, Groceries, Dining, Gas, Medical, Entertainment, Subscriptions, Shopping, Home, Utilities, Kids
Category ordering/grouping for dropdown UX
userStories.testStrategy: CRUD API tests. Deletion constraint test. Seed categories validation.

userStories.title: Auto-categorization rule engine
acceptanceCriteria: Rules table: merchant_pattern (substring match), category_id, created_by (user/system)
On sync, new transactions matched against rules before user sees them
Admin UI to view, create, edit, delete rules
Rule priority: exact match > substring match > Plaid category fallback > uncategorized
Rules applied retroactively on demand: 'Apply rules to all uncategorized' button
Test mode: preview which transactions a rule would match before saving
userStories.testStrategy: Unit tests for pattern matching engine (exact, substring, priority ordering). Integration test: sync + auto-categorize pipeline.

high: Category assignment must be idempotent and handle concurrent edits (Alex and Eric editing same transaction)
medium: Transaction list performance with 12+ months of history — pagination and indexing critical
Mobile UX for category assignment — dropdown may be clunky on iPhone
low: Color picker for categories — can use preset palette instead of free-form hex

preFlightChecklist: Decide: EJS, Handlebars, or plain HTML template strings for server rendering?
Confirm Tailwind CDN version to use (match sibling apps if possible)
Define default category list — use Monarch categories as starting point or simplified set?
